findings.affected_surface: E2 step 4 review.js project filter and foreign-review fixture
findings.claim: The new base-commit existence filter does not establish project ownership. A foreign clone or fork sharing that commit can still contribute review events under this project's project_key.
findings.evidence: E2 step 4 accepts an entry whenever its base commit exists in the project repository. Two repositories with different git common directories can contain the same commit. The added foreign-ledger fixture tests only a base absent from the target repository, so it cannot detect this case. This remains a limitation of the previously non-blocking isolation finding, rather than an unresolved accepted blocker.
findings.evidence_reference: Closure diff: E2 step 4 project-filter addition; E1 fixture foreign-review-ledger addition; unchanged E1 command rule that events of other repositories are never returned.
findings.repair: Before shipping the review reader, bind discovered archive entries to project identity rather than commit existence alone, define handling for legacy entries lacking that identity, and add a foreign-repository fixture that shares the target's base commit.

findings.affected_surface: E3 cursor.js size bound (window_overflow s-halving, e floor); KR-A1.2 late-row guarantee
findings.claim: The diff lowers the w cap from 2000 to 1000 pairs and lets s halve down to 0. Nothing ever restores s to its default. The cursor carries s forward, so once overflow happens the shrunken s is permanent. After that, rows that arrive late are silently dropped on every later poll. KR-A1.2 and E2 step 2 treat late rows as normal for cost and decision sources.
findings.evidence: Changed text: 'When w would exceed the cap the cursor first shrinks s (halving), pruning older pairs ... with s down to 0 only the final ts group could remain'. Unchanged text: next w is pruned to 'ts >= newT - s', and the filter drops 'ts < t - s'. Only the synthetic --since cursor sets s to the default. No rule raises s again. A cap of 1000 pairs over a 300 s window is about 3.3 events/s for one project, which a burst of parallel dispatches with per-turn cost rows reaches. E2 step 2 says cost rows 'can carry ts earlier than rows already read'. With s at 0, any row whose ts is even 1 ms before t but appended after the read is lost, and the only signal is one window_overflow warning on the page that shrank s.
findings.evidence_reference: Plan E3 'Size bound' bullet and 'Next w' bullet; KR-A1.2; E2 step 2; closure diff hunk @@ -221,7 +224,7 @@
findings.repair: Add a recovery rule to the cursor contract. On every page, set the next s to the largest value up to the default (300000) whose pruned w fits the cap. s then shrinks only while the overflow lasts and returns once the window drains. While s is below the default, every response carries window_overflow (or a dedicated slack_reduced code) with the current s. Add a resume test: a 1500-event burst, then quiet pages, assert s returns to 300000 and a late row inside 300 s after recovery is delivered. Add a red-check: never restore s, and the late row is lost.

findings.affected_surface: E1 project and failure rules (project_unresolved JSON); schemas/events.schema.json; consumer table row 'all'; schemas/events.baseline.json
findings.claim: The new project_unresolved stdout object uses the pinned schema string autopilot.events/1 but has none of the envelope's required fields. The schema, the doc consumer table and the baseline gate do not cover it. A consumer that checks only the schema string and then reads events or cursor gets a shape it cannot parse. The shape would also be frozen by accident at merge.
findings.evidence: Diff: 'with --json stdout is {schema:autopilot.events/1, error:{code:project_unresolved}}' and 'project_key stays a required non-null string in the envelope'. E1 consumer rule: consumers 'pin schema == autopilot.events/1'. check-events-contract checks (i)-(v) cover only data shapes, the consumer table and examples.
findings.evidence_reference: Plan E1 'Project and failure rules' (1); §2.6 Consumers; E4 step 2
findings.repair: Define the error object in the schema as a oneOf branch (or give it a distinct schema string such as autopilot.events.error/1). List error.code in the doc and the 'all' consumer row. Add one example and one schema-validation case for it.

findings.affected_surface: E2 step 1 configured-source list ('the git repo'); E2 step 5 qc.js; KR-A1.3 degrade-qc-absent
findings.claim: Two parts of the plan now disagree on what happens when git or the repo is missing. The new rule exits 2 with project_unresolved when cwd is outside a repo or git is not on PATH. E2 step 5 still says 'Missing git or not a repo -> git_unavailable, state degraded' with exit 0. The changed step 1 still lists 'the git repo' as a configured source that yields source_absent. KR-A1.3's 'absent' case for the qc source cannot be built at executable level.
findings.evidence: Diff rule (1) vs unchanged E2 step 5 text, and the diff's own step 1 configured-source list
findings.evidence_reference: Plan E1 'Project and failure rules'; E2 steps 1 and 5; KR-A1.3
findings.repair: Narrow git_unavailable to git failures after the project has resolved (exec failure, timeout, git log error). Remove 'the git repo' from the source_absent list. State that the qc degrade cases are injected through the reader ctx and not through PATH.

findings.affected_surface: E3 size bound ('--since -' stdin); E1 command grammar
findings.claim: The diff introduces '--since -' (cursor read from stdin). The unchanged E1 grammar still says any value other than 0 or an ISO instant is a cursor and that a non-decoding value exits 2 bad_cursor. As written, '-' is rejected.
findings.evidence: Diff: 'The console may also pass it on stdin (--since -)'. E1: '--since <cursor|ISO-8601|0>' and 'Any other value is a cursor; one that does not decode ... exits 2 with bad_cursor'.
findings.repair: Add '-' to the E1 grammar and usage text (read one cursor from stdin, trimmed; empty stdin is a usage error). Add a cursor-* case that passes the cursor on stdin.

findings.claim: The fallback returns 'the input cursor unchanged', but the input is not always a cursor. When --since is omitted, it is 0 or an ISO instant, and the value echoed in the cursor field is undefined. A consumer storing that field may then get bad_cursor on retry, or lose its starting point.
findings.evidence: Diff rule (3): 'the input cursor returned unchanged'. E1: '--since omitted or 0' and '--since <ISO-8601>'.
findings.repair: Specify the fallback cursor for each input form. For a cursor, echo it verbatim. For 0, omitted or ISO, echo the synthetic cursor built from that input (or the literal accepted --since value). Assert this in case (vi-c) for each form.

findings.affected_surface: Consumer table G1 row (basis rendering rule)
findings.claim: The G1 rule fails open. Only basis=self_reported is barred from rendering as verified, while basis is declared an open set. A future or unknown basis value, or a writer bug that omits basis on a self-reported kind, would be rendered as observed state.
findings.evidence: Diff G1 row: 'every data.basis=self_reported value ... must not be rendered as verified state' and 'basis is an open set (an observed value may be added later, additively)'
findings.evidence_reference: Plan E1 consumer table, G1 row
findings.repair: Invert the rule. On kinds that define basis, only an explicitly allow-listed observed value may be rendered as verified. Any other value, including an unknown or missing one, renders as claimed.

findings.claim: The new filter keeps an entry when its base commit exists in the project repo. That does not separate repos that share history, such as separate clones, forks or worktrees-turned-clones of the same upstream. So the added claim that 'a host-wide archive never emits another repo's history' is overstated. Another clone's reviews would appear under this project_key.
findings.evidence: Diff: 'an entry is kept only if its base commit exists in the project repo (git cat-file -e <base>^{commit}) ... so a host-wide archive never emits another repo's history'
findings.repair: Either soften the claim to 'never emits history of repos sharing no commit with this one' and document the shared-history case, or also require the ledger root to come from this project's pointer file, a manifest with matching repo_identity, or an explicit flag or env entry.

findings.claim: The frozen baseline lists fields per kind only, meaning data shapes. Removing or retyping an envelope field (has_more, cursor, generated_at, sources[].state) or an event-level field (ts_basis, root_run_id, source) would still pass the gate. R15 additive-only covers the whole autopilot.events/1 schema.
findings.evidence: Diff: 'written at merge: per kind, each field with JSON type, required or optional, nullable'
findings.repair: Extend the baseline and check (v) to the envelope, the common event fields, sources[] and warnings[] entries. Add a red-check that removes has_more from both schema and doc, and the gate exits 1.
